title: Fixed-Point Uniqueness Conditions

basis.scope: Introduce bounded fixed-point uniqueness conditions for correct continuation fixed points. This patch classifies uniqueness only after correctness and bounded equivalence-class preservation, without asserting universal uniqueness or universal existence.

core_rule.statement: CorrectFix(C) is classified as UniqueFix(C) only when every other correct fixed point in the same ClassFix and bounded evaluation regime belongs to EqClassFix(C); bounded fixed-point uniqueness remains diagnostic, and RT_core remains unchanged.

purpose: Introduce bounded fixed-point uniqueness conditions for correct continuation fixed points. This patch distinguishes uniqueness classification from correctness while leaving universal uniqueness, universal existence, and recovery deferred.

canonical_claims.statement: Fixed-point uniqueness is bounded and applies only after correctness.
EqClassFix(C) captures equivalence under the declared continuation, trace, and fixed-point evaluation semantics.
UniqueFix(C) requires that every other correct fixed point in the same bounded class belong to EqClassFix(C).
FailUniqueFix(C) classifies uniqueness failure without asserting universal uniqueness or universal existence.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Uniqueness
formal_objects.definition: The condition that a correct fixed point is the only continuation fixed point satisfying the declared bounded fixed-point semantics within its fixed-point class and evaluation regime.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Equivalence Class
formal_objects.definition: The class of fixed-point candidates considered equivalent under the declared continuation, trace, and fixed-point evaluation semantics.

formal_objects.name: Fixed-Point Uniqueness Failure
formal_objects.definition: The classified failure state produced when more than one non-equivalent correct fixed point exists within the declared bounded fixed-point class.

uniqueness_rule.statement: CorrectFix(C) is classified as UniqueFix(C) only when every other correct fixed point in the same ClassFix and bounded evaluation regime belongs to EqClassFix(C).

failure_conditions: Semantic preservation does not isolate a single equivalence class representative.
More than one non-equivalent correct fixed point exists in the bounded fixed-point class.
The continuation exits the declared admissible evaluation regime.
non_claims: Does not assert universal fixed-point uniqueness.
Does not assert universal fixed-point existence.
governance_notes: Uniqueness is established only after admissibility and correctness.
Equivalence-class membership is bounded by the declared continuation, trace, and evaluation semantics.
Uniqueness does not imply existence or correctness.
